PHILIPPE I er (1052-1108) roi de France (1060-1108)

Couronné à Reims en 1059 en présence de son père, Philippe I er , fils d'Henri I er (mort en 1060) et d'Anne de Kiev, ne règne seul qu'à partir de 1066, car sa mère, assistée de son oncle, le comte de Flandre Baudouin V, et de l'archevêque de Reims, Gervais, exerce la régence de 1060 à 1066. Sous son règne se dessinent les grandes lignes de la politique des souverains capétiens du xii e siècle : assurer une base réelle à la puissance royale en consolidant le domaine, et abaisser ou contenir les trop puissants vassaux.
Pour reconstituer le domaine royal, il s'empare d'une partie du Vermandois, du Gâtinais (1068), du Vexin français (1077), de la vicomté de Bourges et de la seigneurie de Dun-le-Roi (1101). Il développe l'administration royale aux dépens des seigneurs féodaux, et, pour assurer des revenus à la couronne, il dispose des biens d'Église et vend les charges ecclésiastiques, ce qui lui attire les foudres des réformateurs grégoriens. Au moment où le pape Urbain II prêche en France la première Croisade (1095), Philippe I er est excommunié pour avoir répudié Berthe de Hollande et épousé Bertrade de Montfort.

## Objective
- Turn the standalone Norman Conquest prototype into a coherent, historically grounded, mobile-friendly grand strategy game.
- Validate its seasonal framework, meaningful choices, and manageable scope.

## Requirements
- Preserve standalone `index.html`, the 1066 campaign, and five playable rulers: Harold II Godwinson, Philip I, Constantine X Doukas, Iziaslav I, and Robert Guiscard.
- Use roughly three-month seasonal turns with three major actions, political decisions, player and rival actions, resource updates, events, and turn advancement.
- Keep actions consequential, apply the same fundamental rules to rival realms, and allow plausible alternate histories.
- Retain historical context, citations, map attribution, and uncertainty disclosures.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation inline in `index.html`.
- Use Cliopatria v0.2.1 1066 polity geometry, CC BY 4.0; disclose approximate borders and keep Normandy AI-controlled.
- Treat ruler initials as typographic markers, not historical portraits.
- Use seasonal turns, six shared realm stats, abstract political and military actions, and rival-court AI.
- Keyboard Enter/Space selection should call `chooseRuler` directly rather than `.click()` on an SVG path.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, ruler selection, interactive map, campaign screen, chronicle, citations, attribution, local save/load, settings persistence, and mobile touch pan/pinch.
- Implemented seasonal turns with three actions, six shared realm stats, ruler-specific objectives and internal-pressure profiles, seasonal updates, and rival AI.
- Tested action costs/effects and limits, seasonal advancement and rival actions, save/continue, five ruler initializations, mobile width, menu routing, map selection, mouse pan/zoom, Normandy AI-only behavior, and Harold’s historical marker.
- Fixed action click delegation, historical marker timing, older/malformed save normalization, and invalid calendar dates; inline JavaScript syntax checks pass.
- Constantine and Iziaslav historical markers surface once and explicitly do not force outcomes.
- Settings switches toggle and persist; touch drag/pinch change map transforms.
- Verified Enter and Space select focused map realms; a clean Enter test produced no uncaught exceptions. Follow-up keyboard checks pass.

### Active
- Assess long-term strategic balance: 24-season simulations showed substantial threat growth and levy depletion in some playstyles; policy simulation results need review.
- Review historical claims, citations, map attribution, and uncertainty disclosures; an independent source review is underway.
- Investigate the earlier reported `TypeError: e.target.click is not a function` at `index.html:250`; current source search finds no `target.click`, and clean keyboard tests show no exception.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review the 24-season policy simulation output and determine whether rival pressure or resource sustainability needs tuning.
2. Incorporate the pending historical sourcing review; fix any concrete inaccuracies or unsupported claims.
3. Re-run browser regressions and confirm whether the reported click exception can still be reproduced.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone prototype containing gameplay logic, UI, map, styling, and save/load.
- `/tmp/opencode/policy-check.mjs`: 24-season simulations across five rulers and four policies.
- `/tmp/opencode/real-key-check.mjs`: Clean browser test for Enter-based map selection and uncaught exceptions.
- `/tmp/opencode/keyboard-debug.mjs`: Earlier setup-screen keyboard and exception debugging.
- `/tmp/opencode/followup-check.mjs`: Settings, keyboard/touch controls, historical markers, and balance checks.
- `/tmp/opencode/deep-check.mjs`: Browser regression checks.

## Important Context
- Save key: `ch-norman-save`; core functions include `startGame`, `renderGame`, `performAction`, `endTurn`, and `loadGame`.
- Map attribution: https://github.com/Seshat-Global-History-Databank/cliopatria
- Repository changes remain uncommitted; `index.html`, `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh` are untracked.
- The earlier `deep-check.mjs` settings failure is superseded by follow-up checks that verified both switches toggle and persist.

Roger I (born 1031, Normandy, Fr.—died June 22, 1101, Mileto, Calabria [Italy]) was the count of Sicily from 1072. He was the last son of the second marriage of Tancred of Hauteville.
Roger went to Italy in 1057 to aid his brother Robert Guiscard in his conquest of Calabria from the Byzantines (1060). They began the conquest of Sicily from various Muslim rulers in 1061 with the capture of Messina, and they completed it in 1091. The turning point of the struggle was the capture of Palermo in 1072, when Robert invested Roger as his vassal with the county of Sicily and Calabria with a limited right to govern and to tax. After Robert’s death Roger acquired full right to govern from Robert’s son and in 1098 received the title of apostolic legate from Pope Urban II, which gave him control of the church in Sicily. At his death, Roger had created a centralized, efficient government, where the authority of the count was unchallenged.

## Objective
- Turn the standalone Norman Conquest prototype into a coherent, historically grounded, mobile-friendly grand strategy game.
- Validate its seasonal framework, meaningful choices, and manageable scope.

## Requirements
- Preserve standalone `index.html`, the 1066 campaign, and five playable rulers: Harold II Godwinson, Philip I, Constantine X Doukas, Iziaslav I, and Robert Guiscard.
- Use roughly three-month seasonal turns with three major actions, political decisions, player and rival actions, resource updates, events, and turn advancement.
- Keep actions consequential, apply the same fundamental rules to rival realms, and allow plausible alternate histories.
- Retain historical context, citations, map attribution, and uncertainty disclosures.

## Decisions
- Keep the implementation inline in `index.html`.
- Use Cliopatria v0.2.1 1066 polity geometry, CC BY 4.0; disclose approximate borders and keep Normandy AI-controlled.
- Treat ruler initials as typographic markers, not historical portraits.
- Use seasonal turns, six shared realm stats, abstract political and military actions, and rival-court AI.
- Keyboard Enter/Space selection calls `chooseRuler` directly rather than `.click()` on an SVG path.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented menu, ruler selection, interactive map, campaign screen, chronicle, citations, attribution, local save/load, settings persistence, and mobile touch pan/pinch.
- Implemented seasonal turns with three actions, six shared realm stats, ruler-specific objectives and internal-pressure profiles, seasonal updates, and rival AI.
- Tested action costs/effects and limits, seasonal advancement and rival actions, save/continue, five ruler initializations, mobile width, menu routing, map selection, mouse pan/zoom, Normandy AI-only behavior, and Harold’s historical marker.
- Fixed action click delegation, historical marker timing, older/malformed save normalization, and invalid calendar dates; inline JavaScript syntax check passes.
- Constantine and Iziaslav historical markers surface once and explicitly do not force outcomes.
- Settings switches toggle and persist; touch drag/pinch change map transforms.
- Verified Enter and Space select focused map realms; clean keyboard checks show no uncaught exceptions and the prior `TypeError: e.target.click is not a function` is not reproducible.
- Historical review completed; updated map uncertainty disclosure, softened Philip I’s minority/regency description and added Emily Joan Ward citation, and revised Robert Guiscard’s Sicily chronology and Melfi wording.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Turn the standalone Norman Conquest prototype into a coherent, historically grounded, mobile-friendly grand strategy game.
- Preserve the 1066 campaign and five playable rulers while making seasonal choices, rival actions, and resource management meaningful.

## Requirements
- Keep the implementation inline in standalone `index.html`; retain the 1066 campaign and five playable rulers: Harold II Godwinson, Philip I, Constantine X Doukas, Iziaslav I, and Robert Guiscard.
- Use roughly three-month turns with three major actions, political decisions, player and rival actions, resource updates, events, and turn advancement.
- Keep actions consequential and apply the same fundamental rules to rival realms; allow plausible alternate histories.
- Retain historical context, citations, map attribution, and uncertainty disclosures.

## Decisions
- Use Cliopatria v0.2.1 1066 polity geometry, CC BY 4.0; disclose approximate borders and keep Normandy AI-controlled.
- Treat ruler initials as typographic markers, not historical portraits.
- Use six shared realm stats, abstract political and military actions, and rival-court AI.
- Keyboard Enter/Space selection calls `chooseRuler` directly rather than `.click()` on an SVG path.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the menu, ruler selection, interactive map, campaign screen, chronicle, citations, attribution, local save/load, settings persistence, and mobile touch pan/pinch.
- Implemented seasonal turns, three actions per season, six realm stats, ruler-specific objectives and pressure profiles, seasonal updates, and rival AI.
- Fixed action click delegation, historical marker timing, older/malformed save normalization, and invalid calendar dates; inline JavaScript syntax check passes.
- Historical review updated map uncertainty disclosure, Philip I’s minority/regency description and Emily Joan Ward citation, and Robert Guiscard’s Sicily chronology and Melfi wording.
- Fixed rival pressure simulation so rival courts press claims at most once per season; added seasonal levy recovery capped at 36 and disabled actions that cannot provide a benefit.
- Browser checks passed for settings persistence, Enter/Space map selection, touch pan/pinch, historical markers, 24-season intervention runs, and no uncaught exceptions.
- `index.html` remains untracked; no commit is recorded.

### Active
- Assess strategic balance after the latest economy/rival changes. `/tmp/opencode/policy-after.json` shows passive threat remains high (76–94 after 24 seasons), governance-only play can ignore threat, and military-focused play can exhaust treasury; the tested balanced policy has 65–68 failed action attempts.
- Decide whether further tuning or UX feedback is needed for failed action attempts and the long-run resource/action balance.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect the remaining balance results and determine whether to tune action availability, costs, or strategic pressure further.
2. Run browser regressions and inline JavaScript syntax check after any additional changes.
3. Check `git status` and preserve the uncommitted state.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Standalone game implementation and current balance changes.
- `/tmp/opencode/policy-check.mjs`: 24-season simulations across five rulers and four policies.
- `/tmp/opencode/policy-after.json`: Latest policy simulation results.
- `/tmp/opencode/followup-check.mjs`: Browser checks for settings, keyboard/touch controls, historical markers, balance, and exceptions.
- `/tmp/opencode/real-key-check.mjs`: Clean browser test for Enter-based map selection and uncaught exceptions.

## Important Context
- Save key: `ch-norman-save`; core functions include `startGame`, `renderGame`, `performAction`, `endTurn`, and `loadGame`.
- Map attribution: https://github.com/Seshat-Global-History-Databank/cliopatria
- Latest balance changes: rival courts now press claims at most once per season; player levies recover by two per season up to 36; muster and capped or no-benefit actions are disabled in the UI.
- Other untracked repository files include `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `start.sh`, and `startup.sh`.
